newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures settled little changed on Friday after a calm session and analysts said while Monday looked set to be equally subdued, demand from domestic investors should help French bonds continue to outperform.

While concerns about the state of public finances in France and Germany ensured French bond futures remained capped by resistance at 129.52/54 on Friday, French 10-year bonds outperformed their German counterparts.
Analysts said domestic demand should keep French bonds supported in the event of any U.S. bond declines or if German Bund sales due next week pushed Bund yields higher.

Traders said that although the clear market consensus was for the U.S. Federal Reserve to leave key interest rates unchanged at its policy meeting on July 1-2, caution ahead of the meeting should keep activity subdued on Monday.

Nathalie Fillet, bond analyst at Banque Paribas, said it was interesting French 10-year bonds continued to outperform, the spread under Bunds moved to minus 12 on Friday, due mainly to the fact domestic investors had cash to invest and repayments in the months to come would ensure this situation persisted.
She said the spread could well move to minus 20 basis points in the months to come.
Investors "want to buy but they think (the market's) a bit expensive. They've been waiting for a fall but as it hasn't happened they are buying bit by bit," she said.

An analyst at a French brokerage said if the partial privatisation of France Telecom were given the green light by the new Socialist government it would be positive for the bond market to the extent it could ease pressures on the deficit.
There was little reaction to the admission by the French government that the public deficit would be more than three percent in 1997 on Thursday as most people had already discounted an overshoot.

One traders said after a negative start the French bond market had been supported by switching from peripheral European bond markets back into German bonds but resistance at 129.52 proved too stiff given the lack of volume and positive news.
The September bond future slipped back from a high of 129.54, found support around 129.36 and fluctuated in a narrow range from mid-morning onwards and settled at 129.38.
September PIBOR was equally subdued, trading in a three basis point range and settling down one at 96.59, resistance at 96.61 providing the cap for the session.
The French franc benefitted slightly from a rally in the dollar against the mark and was trading at 3.3725 late on Friday compared with 3.3730 on Thursday.
